title: import-time logging test: run a subprocess with MLFLOW_CONFIGURE_LOGGING=0 and host root logging, then count stderr
answers: How do I write a test that checks an MLflow module emits no logs when imported under a user's own logging config?
Why does my subprocess test still get MLflow's logging handlers even after setting a logging env var?
How do I assert a particular warning text appears exactly once on stderr from a fresh interpreter?
body:
Path: tests/types/test_type_hints.py test for import-time logging of mlflow.types.responses; it launches a fresh interpreter via subprocess.run so module-level code runs once and sees a clean logging setup.
Rule: to test import-time logging, run `sys.executable -c` in a subprocess, configure root logging in the code string with logging.basicConfig before importing the module, copy os.environ, pop MLFLOW_LOGGING_CONFIGURE_LOGGING, and set MLFLOW_CONFIGURE_LOGGING=0 so MLflow does not install its own handlers. Then assert on result.stderr with count() for the expected message and absence checks for the unexpected variant.
Constraints: an in-process test cannot re-trigger module-level imports reliably, so use a subprocess. The test also checks that an ordinary union warning called after import still appears, so the suppression is not over-broad.
applies: Tests that verify warning or log output produced at import time in mlflow modules.
says: Importing the package prints unwanted schema inference warnings to the console output.
Unwanted log messages appear in the terminal when importing under custom logging configurations.
Stop emitting unexpected warning messages to standard error during module import.
Legitimate union type warnings should still be displayed after the initial import.
search: Import-time logging tests in tests/types/test_type_hints.py verify module warning suppression by spawning a subprocess with sys.executable, setting MLFLOW_CONFIGURE_LOGGING=0, and configuring root logging with logging.basicConfig. Applies to tests verifying log or warning output emitted at import time, such as schema inference warnings in mlflow.types.responses. The test pops MLFLOW_LOGGING_CONFIGURE_LOGGING, inspects result.stderr with count() for expected warnings, and asserts that post-import union warnings are not suppressed.
